module.title: Personalities, Character Traits & Feelings
module.objective: Describe character traits, personality qualities, and personal feelings using adjectives like cheerful, polite, honest, shy, and confident.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Friends and Feelings
subModules.grammarFocus: Using am, is, and are with personality adjectives; using because to give a reason
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Personality adjectives and feeling words: cheerful, polite, honest, shy, confident, friendly, helpful, happy

content.summary: In this reading mission, you will read a short text about two friends with different personalities. You will learn how to find the main idea and important details. You will also notice how English uses am, is, and are before adjectives such as cheerful, shy, and confident. Read carefully to learn why people like their friends.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use subject + am/is/are + adjective: She is cheerful. They are kind. Use because + subject + am/is/are + adjective to give a reason.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Personality traits and feelings, including cheerful, polite, honest, shy, confident, friendly, helpful, and happy.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: First, skim the text to understand who the people are and what the text is about. Then, scan the text for names, personality words, and reasons.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short A1 passage about friends and their personalities.
Identify key details, including names, character traits, actions, and feelings.
Recognize and practice am, is, and are with personality adjectives.
Find reasons with because in a short reading text.

contextWarmup.prompt: Your friend always says hello, smiles, and helps people. Which word describes your friend best?
contextWarmup.explanation: A person who smiles and helps people is often cheerful and helpful.

rules: Use am, is, or are before an adjective: I am happy. She is polite. They are friendly.
Use because to give a reason: I like him because he is honest.
A person can have more than one trait: Maya is cheerful and confident.
Look for actions in the text. Actions can show personality: A helpful person helps others.

commonTrap.explanation: Do not forget am, is, or are before a personality adjective. Also, do not choose an answer only because you see one familiar word. Read the full sentence for the meaning.

content.context: Lina introduces two friends to her class and describes their personalities and feelings.
content.text:
Today, Lina introduces her two friends to the class. “This is Maya,” she says. “Maya is cheerful and friendly. She smiles every morning, and she is helpful in class.” Maya feels confident because she knows the answer to a question. She puts up her hand and speaks clearly.

“Next, this is Amir,” Lina says. “Amir is shy, but he is very polite and honest.” Amir does not talk a lot at first. He says, “Hello,” quietly to the class. Then a student drops some books. Amir helps the student and asks, “Are you OK?” Everyone thanks him.

At lunch, Maya shares her fruit with Amir. Amir is happy and smiles. Lina likes both friends because they are kind in different ways. Maya is cheerful and confident, and Amir is polite and helpful.

highlights.note: Confident describes Maya's feeling when she knows an answer.

highlights.text: he is very polite and honest
highlights.note: Use he is before personality adjectives.
Because gives the reason why Lina likes her friends.

content.context: Maya and Rina are at school. They are talking about David, a new student in their class. They describe his personality and talk about his confidence.
content.audioPrompt: Listen carefully to the following dialogue between Maya and Rina. Listen for David's personality and feelings.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Do you know David, the new student in our class?
lines.translation: Apakah kamu kenal David, murid baru di kelas kita?

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Yes, I do! He seems very friendly and polite.
lines.translation: Ya, aku kenal! Dia terlihat sangat ramah dan sopan.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I agree. Why do you like him?

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Because he is always cheerful and helpful to everyone.
lines.translation: Karena dia selalu ceria dan suka menolong semua orang.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That's true. He is also very honest and generous.
lines.translation: Itu benar. Dia juga sangat jujur dan murah hati.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: But I think he is a bit shy when speaking in front of the class.
lines.translation: Tapi aku pikir dia agak pemalu ketika berbicara di depan kelas.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes, but he is becoming more confident now.
lines.translation: Ya, tapi dia menjadi lebih percaya diri sekarang.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: That is good. He speaks more in our English class now.
lines.translation: Itu bagus. Dia sekarang lebih banyak berbicara di kelas bahasa Inggris kami.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes! I hope we can be good friends with him.
lines.translation: Ya! Aku harap kita bisa menjadi teman baik dengannya.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Describe People and Feelings

content.summary: Write simple sentences about a person's personality and feelings. Use a subject, the correct form of be, and an adjective. You can join two adjectives with and or but. Use because to give a reason.

blueprintItems.title: Join Two Traits
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + am / is / are + adjective + and / but + adjective.

blueprintItems.title: Give a Reason
blueprintItems.formula: Sentence + because + subject + am / is / are + adjective.
blueprintItems.example: I like Mia because she is polite.

mechanicsRules.rule: Start every sentence with a capital letter.
mechanicsRules.why: The first word in a sentence needs a capital letter.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a full stop at the end of a statement.
mechanicsRules.why: A full stop shows that the sentence is complete.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use am, is, or are before a personality adjective.
mechanicsRules.why: English sentences need the verb be before an adjective.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use because to introduce a reason.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I like Ben because he is polite.
mechanicsRules.why: After because, write a subject and the verb be.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Talking About Friends and Feelings

content.summary: Talk about your friends with clear, short sentences. Use personality words such as cheerful, polite, honest, shy, and confident. You can also say how a person feels, for example: happy, sad, excited, or tired.
content.audioGuidance: Speak slowly and clearly. Stress the important adjective in your sentence: She is CHEERful. He is conFIdent. Use a falling voice for statements. Use a rising voice for yes or no questions, such as: Is she shy?

pillars.name: Clear Personality Words
pillars.explanation: Practise cheerful, polite, honest, shy, and confident. Make the stressed syllable stronger and longer.

pillars.name: Simple Descriptions
pillars.explanation: Use short patterns: My friend is cheerful. She is honest. He is not shy.

pillars.name: Feelings and Reasons
pillars.target: Say feelings and give one simple reason
pillars.explanation: Use because to explain: I like her because she is helpful. I feel happy because she is kind.

pillars.name: Natural Intonation
pillars.explanation: Let your voice rise at the end of a yes or no question. Let your voice fall at the end of a statement.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: In person, stress the first syllable: PER-son. In personality, stress moves to AL: per-son-AL-i-ty.
Keep the strong beat on KIND in both words. Make the last syllable in kindness short and weak.
Keep the stress on CHEER. Say the final syllables quickly: CHEER-ful-ly.

drills.phonetic: /maɪ best frend ɪz ˈtʃɪəfəl ænd pəˈlaɪt/
drills.hint: Make CHEER strong in cheerful and LITE strong in polite.
Say the h clearly in helpful. Keep honest smooth and clear.

drills.phonetic: /hiː ɪz ʃaɪ bət hiː ɪz ˈveri kaɪnd/
drills.hint: Pause a little before but, then say very kind with a warm voice.

drills.hint: Stress CON in confident and PUB in public.
Let your voice rise on today because this is a yes or no question.

roleplay.context: You are speaking with Mr. Khoirul about your best friend. He asks about your friend's name, personality, and feelings. Describe your friend with simple adjectives and give a reason why you like this person.

turns.text: Hello! Today, let's talk about your best friend. What is your best friend's name?
turns.translation: Halo! Hari ini, mari kita bicara tentang sahabatmu. Siapa nama sahabatmu?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hi, Mr. Khoirul! My best friend's name is Sarah.
turns.translation: Hai, Pak Khoirul! Nama sahabat saya Sarah.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Nice! Can you describe Sarah's personality? What is she like?
turns.translation: Bagus! Bisakah kamu menggambarkan kepribadian Sarah? Seperti apa dia?

turns.text: She is very friendly and cheerful. She always smiles.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That sounds wonderful! Why do you like her?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Because she is honest and helpful. She helps me with my homework.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Excellent! Is she shy or confident?
